Instagram setup checklist

About 30 minutes, once. It protects everything you post afterward. Chapters 7 and 16 of the playbook explain why each step matters.

1. Account type

Switch to a professional account if you haven't: Profile → menu (the three lines) → Account type and tools → Switch to professional account → pick a category.

Creator or Business? Choose Business if you need product tags or a shop, lead forms, an address on your profile, or a tool that requires Business. Otherwise choose Creator. Neither gets more reach, and neither gives you music rights.

2. Four settings that matter

Keep the account public. Private accounts can't be recommended to new people.

Check Account Status (in Settings). It shows whether your account can be recommended to people who don't follow you, and what to fix if not. Check again if your reach suddenly collapses.

Allow search engines: leave "Allow public photos and videos to appear in search engine results" on.

Connect Facebook sharing (section 4).

3. Your profile is your buying hub

Name field says what you do: "Frank | Handyman in Austin."

Bio passes the 10-second test: what you sell, who it's for, the price or "from $__," and what to do next.

First link goes straight to your one next step (a product, booking, quote, or checkout page, never a generic homepage).

Action button (if your booking tool supports one), 3 pinned posts (best proof, clearest offer explainer, most-asked question), and Highlights: "How to buy," "Reviews," "FAQ."

4. Facebook: set it once (5 minutes)

Instagram → Profile → menu (the three lines) → Accounts Center → Connected experiences → Sharing across profiles.

Choose your Instagram account as the source and your Facebook Page as the destination.

Turn on automatic sharing for posts and Reels. Stories are optional: check how yours look on Facebook first.

Confirm your Facebook Reels audience is Public (in Facebook's Reels settings).

After your first few Reels, look at them on Facebook: video, audio and caption. If a Reel's music didn't carry over, reshare it with original or cleared audio.

5. Before you post anything

A folder outside Instagram (Google Drive, Dropbox, or iCloud) for clean master files, carousel source files, photos, hooks that worked, and proof screenshots (with permission).

Your one next step and its exact link, written down.

The phone test done: open your profile as a customer, tap your link, try to buy, book, or request a quote, and fix the first friction point.

Insights location found: Profile → Professional dashboard (account-wide), and "View insights" under any post.

Menu names change. Instagram moves and renames settings from time to time, and they can differ between iPhone and Android. If a step doesn't match your app, search for the setting's name in Settings.
